title: file-facts.json: what the file is (panorama.content/0)
description: Facts about one video file: streams, the timeline rule and frame rate, colour and HDR, Dolby Vision, chapters, the black level, the crop vocabulary and text found in the bars. Written by the pre-scan (everything except the parts marked as filled by the full scan) and updated when the scan has been through the film.

container.description: ffprobe format name, for example matroska,webm.

video.description: The video stream the performer decodes (the one libavformat's best-stream choice picks).

stream_index.description: Absolute stream index in the container.

width.description: Stored width in pixels (the decoder's output, not the displayed width).

sample_aspect_ratio.description: Width of a stored pixel over its height; displayed width = width * sar. Positions in the model are in stored pixels, so the planner applies this.

rotation_deg.description: Display-matrix rotation from the container; positions are in the unrotated stored frame.

color_range.description: tv (limited, 16-235) or pc (full). Luma columns of signals.bin keep the stream's own code values.

mastering_display.description: SMPTE ST 2086 values as the file states them, luminance in cd/m2 (nits).

dolby_vision.description: Null when the stream has no Dolby Vision configuration record. Level 5 (active area) and level 1 (brightness) blocks are frame side data that FFmpeg's libavutil delivers through av_dovi_find_level; ffprobe and showinfo print scene_refresh_flag but not those blocks.

level5_active_area.description: Active-area offsets in pixels (left, right, top, bottom) when sampled; null when not sampled.

timeline.description: The timeline convention made concrete for this file: the time base, the first frame's timestamp, the frame count and rate. The frame table itself is the columns pts and key of signals.bin.

kind.description: linear: the file's own timeline as FFmpeg demuxes it. MKV ordered chapters and segment links are not followed (FFmpeg ignores them); a file that uses them is described as its plain linear timeline.

rule.description: The exact rule, in words, turning pts ticks into seconds; same as common.schema.json.

first_pts_ticks.description: pts of frame 0 in ticks; time zero. May be negative or large (MP4 empty edits, MKV starting at 10 s): the rebasing removes it.

first_pts_s_abs.description: pts[0] * tb in seconds on the container's own timeline; subtitle and chapter times are converted to the rebased timeline by subtracting it.

duration_s.description: From frame 0's time to the end of the last frame.

fps_avg.description: (frames - 1) / (time of last frame - time of first frame).

nominal_rate.description: The standard rate (24000/1001, 25, ...) within 1% of fps_avg (or 0.5% of the median step); null when none fits.

vfr.description: True when more than 0.5% of the frames lie off the regular grid of the nominal rate by more than max(1.5 ms, 2 ticks) (a dropped frame or a 30 / 60 fps stretch moves everything after it off the grid; timestamps rounded to a millisecond do not); without a nominal rate, when more than 0.5% of the steps differ from the median step by more than 1.5 ticks.

step_histogram.description: The most common steps between consecutive frames, in ticks and ms, with counts.

frame_table_source.description: packets: built from the container's packet list (no decoding) and verified against the performer's decoder path; synthetic: the stream has no timestamps (raw .264 / .hevc), frames are numbered at the stream's rate and the performer would show one frame.

frame_table_stats.description: Packets seen, packets dropped (flagged to be discarded by an edit list, without a timestamp, or repeating one), frames kept.

ordered_chapters.description: Matroska only: whether the file asks for a timeline other than its own (ordered chapter editions, chapters that link other files). Null for other containers. Neither FFmpeg nor this model follows them.

streams.description: Every stream of the container, summarised. Subtitle streams carry subtitle_kind: text (parsed and rendered) or bitmap.

analyzer_versions.description: Versions of the signal groups and tables this folder was made with.

black_level.description: What the bars of this file are made of, estimated from the keyframes (research: the cropdetect threshold must sit just above it). Values are 8-bit code values of the decoded stream.

nominal.description: 16 for video range, 0 for full range.

bar_level.description: Median of the flat dark edges found; the nominal level when none.

bright_threshold.description: bar_level + 40: a pixel at or above it in a bar is text or a logo.

crop_vocabulary.description: The file's few real picture rectangles (research: one to three modes) with their share of the evidence. From keyframes after the pre-scan, from every shot after the scan.

text_in_bars.description: Per side, how much burned-in text or logo was found in the bars (filled by the full scan): frames that had a bar on that side, frames with text, their share, and the largest extension of the crop that was needed to keep the text.

slide_region_of_interest.description: The part of the picture used to measure camera slides: the intersection of the picture rectangles of the main crop modes, in the 480x270 analysis grid (the whole grid when the file has no bars).
